label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Handover for Thursday's launch

Inês,

I'm leaving tonight and I don't know for how long. My father is ill and I'm going to be with my family. That's all I'll say about it here, but it means you're running Thursday without me.

I'm sorry. I found the mistake in figure 3 only this afternoon, and I'm handing you a mess that is entirely mine, at the worst possible moment. You didn't make it, and you shouldn't have to carry it. Below is everything I know, in the order I'd do it.

**What went wrong**

Figure 3 and the summary used the 2030 revenue estimate from an old run, one where the free allocation phase-out wasn't applied. The correct 2030 LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. The conclusion of the paper doesn't change, but the headline number does.

Where things stand:
- PDF v7 on the drive is corrected (pages 3, 14 and 15).
- Deck v4 is not corrected. Slides 6 and 9 need the new number. Check my speaker notes too, in case 2.1 appears there.
- The press release is not corrected. Hanna sent it on Friday to our 34 Brussels contacts, embargoed until Thursday 10:00 CET, and it says 2.1.

My note "ERROR figure 3 - must fix before launch" in the launch folder has the same details.

**What to do, in order**

1. Tomorrow (Tuesday), fix slides 6 and 9 in the deck. You know the deck better than I do now, so I trust you to catch anything else that leans on the old figure.

2. Talk to Hanna tomorrow about a corrected press release. It needs to go to the same 34 contacts, clearly flagged as a correction, and I'd want it out before the journalists' calls on Wednesday at 14:00, and in any case well before the embargo lifts at 10:00 on Thursday. If Hanna needs a senior name on it, Geert can sign it off. He knows I'm away.

3. Reply to Tomás Reyes at Lindqvist's office. He wrote to me today with a timing change: the MEP has a vote moved into Thursday lunchtime and has to leave at 13:30. He asked for the presentation to be 15 minutes instead of 20, and for the panel to start at 12:50. She wants to take at least two questions herself before she goes. I haven't seen a new closing time, so please check with him how he wants to run the end of the session. Please also tell him you're taking my place on the presentation and the panel.

4. Send Tomás the final names for badges by Wednesday 12:00 at the latest. He told me security won't let anyone in otherwise. Include yourself and anyone else from our side who is coming. Don't leave this until the last minute, because it's the one deadline that can't be fixed on the day.

5. Wednesday afternoon: the two journalists' background calls, 14:00 and 15:00, by phone, 20 minutes each. One is from a trade newsletter and one from a Belgian daily. Hanna is confirming them. I'd like you to take them, with Hanna around if she wants to be. Both of them have the old number in the release, so tell them about the correction yourself at the start of the call and give them the right figure. It's much better they hear it from you than find it later.

6. Let Abena Owusu-Mensah know about the new panel start time (12:50) and that you are taking my seat. Her remote link is in the calendar invite and you tested it with her already. Also let Florian Kessler know, so nobody is surprised on the day.

7. Cut your 15 minutes from the 14-slide deck. I'd keep the revenue chart on slide 9 and the LDC message, and trim from the methods end. But you know what matters, so cut it the way you think is right.

**Thursday, the day itself**

Guests should be at the security entrance of the Altiero Spinelli building by 12:00, and Tomás collects the badges. There's a light lunch outside the room from 12:00. Lindqvist welcomes at 12:30, then your presentation, then the panel with Abena, Kessler and you, moderated by Lindqvist.

My view on the mistake: say it yourself, early, in one sentence. Something like, "You may have seen 2.1 billion in the embargoed release; the correct figure for 2030 is 1.4 billion, and the paper has been corrected." Then move on. If anyone asks how it happened, the answer is simple: the mistake is mine, I used the wrong model run. Say so plainly. It is not yours, and nobody should leave thinking it is. It doesn't change what the paper says.

**Kessler**

His comments are in the folder ("Comments on draft (AESU)"), and my reply lines are in "Reply lines for Kessler". The short version:

- He will go after the 80% pass-through assumption in section 4. It's the central case. Annex B runs 40% and 60% as well. You ran those sensitivity runs yourself, so you know them better than anyone. The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. Say that openly, without getting defensive. It's a strength of the paper that we show it.
- On resource shuffling: we agree it's a risk. It's in section 5.2, and we recommend the Commission's monitoring report.

He will probably try to turn the whole panel into a debate about 80%. Don't let him set the tone. Answer the point once, clearly, and bring it back to what the paper is actually about, which is who pays at the border and what that means for the least developed countries. Abena was strong on the call and will probably back us on the LDC side.

**Geert**

Geert knows I'm away. If anything needs a senior decision, go to him. That includes sign-off on the corrected release if Hanna wants it.

**After Thursday**

Lucy Tran from the Halvorsen Foundation is coming with a colleague. For their grant report, she needs two photos from the event and the attendance numbers, ideally by 4 December. Please say hello to her on the day, and send her those things when you have them. It doesn't need to be you personally if you'd rather hand it to someone else.

**Reaching me**

You can call me. But from 9:00 tomorrow (Tuesday) I might not pick up, so please don't count on me for anything. If something really blocks you, leave a message and I'll answer when I can. Everything above should be enough to run on without me.

**One more thing**

I trust you completely. You know this paper as well as I do. You ran the annex B sensitivity runs, you built the deck, and you will be fine in that room. I remember Lisbon, at the COP side event, when the projector died and you rescued my panel without anyone noticing there had been a problem. You are better live than you think. That is why I'm not worried about Thursday, even though I hate not being there.

Thank you, and again, I'm sorry.

Marieke
